tweets.text:
#EXCLUSIVE @CBP officers in Presidio, Texas seized multiple firearms—including machine gun barrels—before they could be smuggled into Mexico.

During a southbound inspection at the Presidio Port of Entry on July 8th, U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers uncovered 6 rifles, 2 handguns, 180 magazines, 500 rounds of ammunition, and firearm components, including machine gun barrels for the M249 light machine gun, hidden inside a 2013 Nissan X-Trail headed for Mexico.

CBP says non-intrusive inspection technology detected anomalies in the vehicle, leading officers to hidden compartments containing the weapons and ammunition.

The driver, a Mexican citizen and lawful U.S. permanent resident, was arrested and charged with smuggling goods and firearms trafficking.

The seizure comes as CBP sources say the area across the border in Ojinaga, Chihuahua, remains the site of a violent turf war between La Línea and factions of the Sinaloa Cartel, as both organizations compete for control of the strategically important Ojinaga smuggling plaza. The rivalry has fueled years of violence in the region, making southbound weapons interdictions a key part of disrupting cartel operations.

Ray Provencio, Director of the El Paso Field Office saying, “This seizure demonstrates CBP’s commitment to preventing firearms and ammunition from illegally entering Mexico and arming dangerous criminal organizations… Our southbound inspection teams search for firearms, ammunition, and currency from illicit criminal activities to prevent this contraband from arming and financing the Mexican Drug cartels. And by doing so we assist our Government of Mexico law enforcement partners as we work to make our shared border region safer.”
